lines.line: node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints Hello, <name>! in upper case, for example HELLO, ADA!
lines.evidence: Right now bin/greet.js skips every --flag, so `--shout Ada` prints 'Hello, Ada!'. A build that leaves that alone fails the line. A build that upper-cases the name only ('Hello, ADA!') also fails, because the line asks for the whole greeting in upper case and gives the exact text HELLO, ADA!. A build that only works when --shout comes after the name does not meet the stated order '--shout <name>'. I could not find a wrong build that meets this line.

lines.line: node bin/greet.js <name> without --shout still prints Hello, <name>!
lines.evidence: I tried a build that always shouts, and one that breaks the plain path, for example by changing how the name is picked out of argv. Both print something other than 'Hello, Ada!' for `node bin/greet.js Ada`, so the run proof fails them. The existing 'cli' test in test/greet.test.js also guards this case.

lines.line: docs/index.md documents the --shout option with an example
lines.evidence: docs/index.md has only one short usage block, so any --shout text in that file sits next to the existing usage, as the request asks. A build that documents --shout only in README.md, or in a new docs page, fails because the line names docs/index.md. A build that mentions the flag without an example fails the words 'with an example'. Nothing about publishing or pages.yml is needed, which matches the non-goal.

lines.line: npm test passes and includes a test that runs node bin/greet.js --shout Ada and asserts it prints HELLO, ADA!
lines.evidence: I tried a build whose test only unit-tests a shout helper in src/greet.js. It fails, because the line says the test must run node bin/greet.js --shout Ada. A test that runs the command but checks something weaker than the output HELLO, ADA! fails the 'asserts it prints HELLO, ADA!' part. npm test is `node --test` and can be run on the PR branch before merge. With this test in place, a build that never wires the flag into bin fails npm test.

result.wrong_build: The closest I came: docs/index.md adds a --shout example whose shown output is wrong or messy (for example 'Hello, ADA!'), while the code and tests are correct. Line 3 asks only that docs/index.md document the option with an example; it does not say the example's output must be right. A careful reader would still count a wrong example as not documenting the option. I could not find a build that meets every line and still clearly misses the request.

The harness refused my result: it says run `clean-shout-1:0.challenge` had already returned its result before this call. There was nothing to fix, so I did not call again, and my verdict was not the one recorded.

My verdict was **PASS** on all four lines of issue #12. I read the repository and changed nothing.

- **`--shout` prints in upper case:** passes. Today `bin/greet.js` ignores every `--` flag, so `--shout Ada` prints `Hello, Ada!` and a build that never adds the flag fails. So does one that upper-cases only the name, because the line asks for the exact text `HELLO, ADA!`.
- **Plain greeting unchanged:** passes. A build that always shouts, or that changes how the name is read, fails the `node bin/greet.js Ada` run. The existing CLI test in `test/greet.test.js` also covers this.
- **Docs in `docs/index.md` with an example:** passes. The file has only one short usage block, so anything added there sits next to it. Docs put only in `README.md` or a new page fail.
- **Test that runs `--shout Ada`:** passes. A test that only checks the greeting function fails, because the line says the test must run `node bin/greet.js`. `npm test` can be run on the branch before merge.

The closest wrong build I found: correct code and tests, but a docs example that shows the wrong output (for example `Hello, ADA!`). The docs line doesn't say the example must be correct. I still counted it as covered, because a careful reader would not call a wrong example documentation.
